run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-259 had issues on November 20, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: Only the Loki source answered in this Run; Prometheus, Jaeger and the Kubernetes API all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt, so pod status, restart counts, K8s events, error-rate and latency series could not be inspected. From the application logs that were available: pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 (namespace app-259, job/service payment-api) logged 8 ERROR lines 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' between 2026-11-20T13:46:00Z and 2026-11-20T14:44:00Z, with wait_time_ms rising from 1227 to 4840 and queue_length between 5 and 15. Before 13:46 the same pod logged only INFO 'Payment processed successfully' lines (latest at 13:42), and INFO successes are interleaved during the burst (13:59) and continue after it (14:49, 15:27; only INFO from 15:27 through 05:32 next day). So the payment-api pod stayed up and kept completing some payments while its database connection pool was exhausted. Which database or dependency it could not get a connection to, and what triggered the exhaustion (dependency slowness, pool configuration, or load), is not established by the evidence: no dependency logs exist in Loki (the only job recorded there is payment-api), and the metrics/traces/Kubernetes sources that could show it were unavailable. No root-cause object is therefore provable.

claims.text: Pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 in namespace app-259 (labels job=payment-api, service=payment-api) logged 8 ERROR lines with message 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' at 13:46, 13:54, 14:03, 14:15, 14:19, 14:21, 14:31 and 14:44 UTC on 2026-11-20; the same lines carry wait_time_ms 1227, 2104, 1495, 2965, 4005, 4840, 2358, 3836 and queue_length 10, 11, 8, 9, 10, 8, 15, 5 respectively.

In the window 2026-11-20T06:39:40Z to 13:45:00Z the same namespace returned only INFO 'Payment processed successfully' lines from pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 (timestamps 06:40, 11:19, 11:40, 11:44, 12:57, 13:42); no ERROR line appears before 13:46, so the 'pool exhausted' error burst begins at 13:46, just after the 13:45 report time.

The failure severity inside the burst increased over time: wait_time_ms for acquiring a database connection went from 1227 ms at 13:46 to 2104 ms at 13:54 and 4840 ms at 14:21, while queue_length ranged 5 to 15, i.e. requests were queuing for a connection for up to ~4.8 s before failing.

The pod kept serving successfully through and after the burst: INFO 'Payment processed successfully' at 13:59 (during the error burst) and at 14:31-to-16:00 window 14:49 and 15:27, and from 15:27:01Z to 2026-11-21T05:32Z only 14 INFO success lines were recorded with no ERROR line.

Loki holds no logs for any dependency of payment-api: a count_over_time over {namespace=~".+"} for 2026-11-20T18:39:40Z to 2026-11-21T06:39:40Z returned exactly one series (namespace=app-259, job=payment-api, 12 lines), and selectors for job=~'.*db.*|.*postgres.*|.*mysql.*|.*database.*' in 13:00-14:30 returned no data, so the database that the pool could not hand out connections to is not identified by any log in this data source.

The pod was not down or crash-looping in the log evidence: it emitted successful payment lines before (13:42), during (13:59) and after (14:49, 15:27) the burst, so the symptom is intermittent connection-acquisition failure inside the running process rather than the pod being unavailable; no restart, OOMKilled or probe-failure line appears in the logs returned for the window.

Most likely the payment-api connection pool was exhausted because its database dependency became slow or stopped releasing connections: the error text names database connection acquisition as the failing step and wait_time_ms grew from 1227 ms to 4840 ms across the burst while queue_length stayed at 5-15, a pattern of downstream unresponsiveness. This remains a hypothesis: the database's own logs are absent from Loki and the Prometheus/Jaeger series that would show dependency latency and error rates were unavailable, so the dependency itself was never observed.

A payment-api side cause (connection-pool size or timeout configuration, or a code/connection-leak path) could equally exhaust the pool at ~13:46 without any dependency problem; this candidate could not be tested because ConfigMaps/Deployments and metric series for in-flight connections were not reachable in this Run.

A load-driven cause (a traffic increase around 13:45 saturating a fixed connection pool) is also possible, consistent with a queue of up to 15 waiters; request-rate metrics (app_payment_transactions_total, traces_span_metrics_calls_total) and traces were unavailable, so volume before versus during the burst was not measured.

Check the payment-api dependency's latency/error series (rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket by rpc_service/rpc_method, plus any database exporter metrics) around 13:45-14:45 to determine whether the database was slow or unreachable, and check pod restart counts, last termination reasons, events and the pool-related ConfigMap entries of the payment-api workload.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable throughout: get_metric_names, get_label_values, metrics_range_query and execute_prometheus_instant_query all returned status=error, reason=SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency or app_payment_transactions_total series were read and no baseline for the payment-api latency exists.

Jaeger was unreachable throughout: traces_list_services, traces_search and traces_search_by_tags returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so callers of payment-api, span error status and the dependency call edge could not be observed.

The Kubernetes API was unreachable throughout: kubernetes_jq_query, kubernetes_tabular_query, kubernetes_count and fetch_pod_logs returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so pod status, restart counts, last termination reason/exit code, K8s events, Deployment/ReplicaSet ownership, ConfigMaps and the cluster-state view of app-259 were not checked.

The database/dependency that the exhausted pool was acquiring connections to is not identified: no dependency logs exist in Loki (only job=payment-api is recorded) and the exact database host/service name is not stated in the error text.

The trigger of the 13:46 onset is unknown: no change, restart, config change or traffic spike was observed. The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so change chronology could not be consulted.

The scope of impact beyond this single pod is unverified: the evidence shows only pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12, which is the only pod name appearing in Loki for this namespace; whether sibling pods or callers such as checkout/frontend failed is unknown.

Whether the errors truly stopped or merely stopped being logged after 14:44 is unknown: the ERROR stream's rolling counts end at about 15:43 and no ERROR line is returned after 14:44, but log retention/ingest gaps cannot be excluded.
next_steps: Query the database/dependency's own metrics and logs (including any postgres/redis exporter and networkpolicy/service/endpoints state) for 13:30-15:00 UTC to see whether it slowed or rejected connections.
Inspect the payment-api Deployment/ReplicaSet, pod events, container last termination reason and restart count, and its ConfigMap pool settings for a change at ~13:45 UTC.
Compare payment-api request volume and error rate before 13:45 with 13:45-14:45 from traces and app_payment_transactions_total to test the load-driven hypothesis.
Confirm whether other payment-api replicas and upstream callers (checkout, frontend) show their own errors in the same window, so impact scope can be stated with evidence.
